analysis:
MARKET REGIME: SPY is mixed — slightly below SMA50 but with a positive 20-day slope, meaning the tape is indecisive. This is not an environment to aggressively deploy capital; selectivity is paramount.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW:
• AMP (-9.19%, $9,440): Critically, AMP does NOT appear in today's screened candidates — it likely failed the confirmed-downtrend filter. A stock absent from the quality+trend screen at -9.19% is a thesis-break signal. The original thesis needs hard scrutiny; if stop has not been hit yet, it should be tightened now to protect against further deterioration. Recommend reviewing stop placement and being prepared to exit.
• NVDA (-2.33%, $14,928): In the candidate list as MIXED/SIDEWAYS extending, -4.7% below SMA50. Small loss, thesis intact (AI capex cycle), but technicals are soft. Hold with existing stop; do not add.
• FOXA (+5.31%, $22,256): Working. Hold.
• ULTA (+13.82%, $10,156): Working well, approaching prior target territory (ULTA previously hit +16% target). Consider trailing stop to lock in gains.

PERFORMANCE CONTEXT: 25% win rate and 0.89 profit factor are sobering — the strategy is not creating alpha over baseline. This demands we be very selective and only act on genuinely asymmetric setups. The correct response is NOT to force activity but to apply strict discipline.

NEW TRADES: One high-conviction setup stands out — ADBE. Forward P/E of 9.84 and PEG of 0.62 for a 34.8% operating margin, $9.3B FCF business is an extraordinary valuation dislocation. Price is basing above both SMA50 and SMA200 at 46% of 52w range. The SMA50 slope is barely negative (-0.6%), so entry should be staged — buy on mild pullback or as SMA50 slope turns positive. Earnings are 47 days out (Dec 9), allowing time for the position to develop before the next catalyst. No other candidate clears the bar of asymmetric setup + quality + reasonable trend. Energy names (VLO, MPC, APA, EOG, OXY) are all above 88% 52w range — late cycle, avoid. NTAP at 82% is borderline extended. CRM at 88% is too extended. Cash preservation remains the priority.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $268 on a mild pullback toward SMA50, or enter at market if price holds above SMA50 for 2+ consecutive sessions AND SMA50 20-day slope turns positive. Do not chase above $274.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Adobe is a dominant software franchise (Creative Cloud, Document Cloud, Experience Cloud) with a 34.8% operating margin, $9.3B in FCF, 61.9% ROE, and 12.9% revenue growth — yet it trades at a forward P/E of 9.84 and a PEG of 0.62. This is an extreme valuation discount relative to business quality, likely reflecting AI-disruption fear that the market has over-priced in. The company is actively embedding AI (Firefly) into its moat-protected subscription base. Analyst EPS revisions are flat (+0.5%) but not deteriorating, and earnings are 47 days out — enough runway before the next catalyst. TECHNICAL: Price is at 46% of the 52-week range, above both SMA50 (+5.7%) and SMA200 (+7.1%), basing in MIXED/SIDEWAYS mode. SMA50 slope is barely negative at -0.6% — this is the transition zone between Stage 1 base and Stage 2 uptrend. Entry at a pullback to the $268 area offers an attractive risk/reward before trend confirmation is fully in place. The 'falling knife' risk is limited because price is already above SMA200 — this is a basing pattern, not a downtrend.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) price closes below $253.50 stop on volume; (2) thesis breaks — meaning FCF decelerates sharply, net revenue retention deteriorates materially, or AI substitution evidence becomes concrete in subscriber metrics; (3) December earnings reveal revenue miss + guidance cut, re-evaluate immediately post-print; (4) if position reaches $325 target, reassess — trail stop to entry if still in position. Time stop: if price is flat or lower 3 months post-entry with deteriorating technicals, exit regardless of price.
